CC: "I can't catch my breath and my heart is racing."

HPI: 64-year-old woman with history of asthma who presents with acute shortness of breath and wheezing that started 6 hours ago after exposure to dust at work. She used her albuterol inhaler 4 times with minimal relief. Associated chest tightness. No fever, no sputum change, no chest pain. She was intubated for asthma 3 years ago.

PMH: Asthma, allergic rhinitis.

Meds: Fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 1 puff BID; Albuterol 2 puffs q4h PRN; Montelukast 10 mg nightly; Loratadine 10 mg daily.

SH: Never smoker. Works as a school custodian. No pets.

ROS: Wheezing, dyspnea, chest tightness. Denies fever, cough, sputum.

PE:
VS: T 98.2 F, HR 118, BP 142/88, RR 28, SpO2 90% on RA.
General: Anxious, tripoding.
Lungs: Diffuse expiratory wheezes, poor air movement.
CV: Tachycardic.
Skin: No rash.

Data:
ABG: pH 7.32, pCO2 48, pO2 68 on room air.
Labs: WBC 9.8, Lactate 2.1.
CXR: Hyperinflated lungs, no focal infiltrate.

A: 64-year-old woman with severe acute asthma exacerbation.

P:
Problem 1: Severe asthma exacerbation
- Continuous albuterol nebs, magnesium 2g IV
- Methylprednisolone 125 mg IV
- ICU evaluation given prior intubation

Problem 2: Hypoxemia and hypercapnia
- O2 to maintain SpO2 92-95%
- Serial ABGs, BiPAP if tiring
